Steps to Reproduce:
1. Launch Minecraft and create a new world with cheats enabled.  
2. Open the chat and run ``/summon hoglin ~ ~ ~ {Attributes:[{Base:0.5d,Name:"generic.attackDamage"}],Age:0}``.  
3. Run ``/gamemode survival`` to switch to Survival mode.  
4. Walk toward the summoned hoglin until it is close enough to attempt an attack.  
5. Wait a few seconds for the hoglin to initiate its attack.  
6. Observe that the game crashes (the client/server stops and a crash report is generated).
Observed Behavior: When an adult hoglin whose generic.attackDamage attribute has been set to a low value (for example 0.5) is summoned with the command /summon hoglin ~ ~ ~ {Attributes:[{Base:0.5d,Name:"generic.attackDamage"}],Age:0} and the player switches to survival mode, the hoglin will attack the player and the server will crash instantly. The crash occurs during the entity tick and the crash report shows an IllegalArgumentException with the message “bound must be positive” generated by java.util.Random.nextInt. The stack trace lists classes such as bae.B, aou.a, apf.a, anv.e, ang.b and continues through the server main loop, indicating that the error originates in the hoglin’s attack handling code. The crash file is named crash‑2020‑03‑11_19.25.11‑server.txt and was reproduced on snapshot 20w11a. Developers have noted that the issue also appears when a baby hoglin matures into an adult while retaining the low attack‑damage attribute, suggesting that the attribute value is not being clamped before the attack calculation. As a result any attempt to engage a hoglin with this modified attack damage causes an immediate server shutdown.
Expected Behavior: When an adult hoglin with its generic.attackDamage attribute set to 1 attacks a target, the hoglin should simply perform its melee attack, dealing the configured amount of damage (or the default damage if the attribute is overridden), and the game should continue running without any crash or error.
